course_name_original: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
course_name_en: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
prerequisites: Spanish language knowledge at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write an understandable informational and argumentative text on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical of the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present their conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they relate to industry-specific issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Can use grammatical constructions, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow for understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry-specific topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Spanish B-2 - compulsory course of 135 hours - semester 2/3: Classes within the module are conducted in the form of exercises (135 hours).
GRAMMATICAL ISSUES: Noun
Verbal nouns
Nouns derived from adjectives
Personal pronoun: functions, omission, order, form
As subject to achieve clarity, emphasis, express opposition
As direct object (DO); allowed forms; use when DO precedes the predicate
As indirect object (IO); use despite the presence of a noun, duplication in evaluative constructions
with preposition (entre, excepto, salvo, incluso, hasta segun+ pron.pers. sujeto)
order and form of IO+DO
Reflexive pronoun: functions
use in impersonal statements; meaning of reciprocity; modification of the meaning of some verbs (quedarse, irse, tomarse)
Adjective
Formation of adjectives with opposite meaning
Compound adjectives
Adjective order and shortened forms
Preposition
Use of 'por' and 'para'
Specific use of prepositions in conjunction with certain verbs and in prepositional phrases
Verb
Functions of impersonal forms (infinitivo, infinitivo compuesto, participio, gerundio)

Morphology and applications of indicative mood tenses [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito indefinido, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto, futuro simple i futuro compuesto de indicativo]
Morphology and applications of conditional mood tenses [condicional simple, condicional compuesto]
Morphology and applications of subjunctive mood [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo]
Passive voice [ser+ participio (+ por + agente)]
Use of periphrastic constructions [e.g.: Estar+participio, Estar+gerundio, acabar+ de+infinit., terminar + de + infinit., volver + a + infinit., llevar + gerundio, ir+ gerundio]
Formation of impersonal constructions
Correlation of tenses in subordinate clauses
Use of verbs 'ser', 'estar', 'haber'
More important verbs changing meaning depending on the voice (e.g.: poner/ ponerse, quedar/ quedarse) and the word accompanying them (e.g.: ponerse + a, ponerse + de).

Words and expressions indicating logical connections between parts of a sentence (simple, complex), ensuring coherence of speech (oral or written), reflecting the speaker's attitude to the presented content (in discussion)

Presenting one's own opinion, providing information from other sources, clarifying, organizing speech and adding new arguments, emphasizing a previously given argument, introducing new counterarguments, contrasting elements, ordering information, correcting information, rephrasing, summarizing, explaining/justifying, citing examples, citing reasons.
expressing assumption, hypothesis, condition, concession, cause, effect
defining temporal relations (sequence, precedence, simultaneity, specific moment or period, initial or final moment, duration)
Reported speech: transformation of individual elements of a sentence/utterance; semantics of verbs denoting an act of communication.
Creating comparisons and absolute superlative

THEMATIC AND VOCABULARY: The issues presented below reflect various aspects of human functioning in society and directly or indirectly contribute to the development of vocabulary and phraseology necessary for the student to succeed in an academic or professional environment. They develop the ability to understand written or oral text and consciously, thoughtfully construct statements on professional and academic topics (from the perspective of one's own education) and general topics, which constitute a universal basis for understanding among people at a given level of education.
Professional work: requirements, skills, experiences, expectations and fears, forms of contact with employer and team
Education. My university, faculty and field of study, subjects and forms of classes
Student life (study, norms, duties and limitations, entertainment, additional development opportunities, individual and group work)
Designing products that meet specific requirements (object, place, etc.)
Means and methods of information transfer in the modern world
Political and historical events
Culture: films, performances, readings
Global problems and problems of local communities
Cities: history, attractions, infrastructure, culture, gastronomy
Customs, holidays, local and international traditions
Travel, tourism, tourism industry
State of the natural environment
Pro-health behaviors, physical activity, extreme sports
Interpersonal relationships and lifestyle: family, friends, formal and informal groups, subcultures
Psychological reactions to events and challenges, attitude to incomprehensible phenomena

LANGUAGE FUNCTIONS and OTHER SKILLS: The functions presented in detail below are components of two broad areas: creating longer individual utterances (oral or written, informational, argumentative or mixed) and participating in a conversation with one or more partners (discussion, debate, meeting, job interview). In both cases, the goal is to develop the ability to present one's professional profile and knowledge in a balanced and professional manner and to take an active stance in situations typical of academic and professional environments.
Provide information, indicate, specify, define, describe; ask for information, provide and supplement information, ask for confirmation and refer to information provided
Ask for opinion/assessment and express opinion/assessment
Express approval/disapproval, support or lack of support
Express agreement/disagreement; ask someone for agreement, encourage agreement
Show doubt
Present arguments and counterarguments
Express certainty/obviousness or their absence
Formulate hypotheses
Express possibility, probability
Express conditions and requirements
Present goals and reasons
Express necessity or need or their absence
Ask about knowledge of something; express knowledge or its absence
Ask about skills and experiences and present them to the interlocutor
Ask about likes and interests and present them
Ask about preferences and define preferences; express indifference or lack of preference
Ask about desires/wishes and present them
Ask about plans and intentions and present them

Ask about emotional experiences and express joy, satisfaction, sadness, boredom, satiety, aversion, anger, indignation, fear, anxiety, concern, sympathy, encouragement, hope, disappointment, resignation, remorse, shame, surprise, wonder, admiration and pride
Define physical sensations
Give commands or instructions
Ask for kindness, an object, help; offer help in action
Make a request/application/petition and respond
Ask for permission, grant/deny permission; forbid
Propose and suggest solutions, joint actions
Offer, propose and invite; accept an offer or invitation or refuse
Advise, warn, threaten
Reproach
Make promises and express commitment
Calm and comfort
Present goals and reasons
Formulate conditions and requirements
Edit texts: private and official emails and letters, e.g. cover letter, CV, applications, petitions, complaints, reports
Respond in writing or orally to oral texts (interviews, general conversations, as well as popular science statements)
Read popular science texts with understanding.
Create and present longer oral statements related to the field of study
assessment_rules: A condition for passing is to receive a positive grade from all colloquiums conducted during the semester. If a negative grade is received, the student has the right to retake it: a retake of a negative grade from the first attempt results in the negative grade being cancelled and replaced by a positive grade counting towards the average. A retake of a grade from the second attempt results in the average of the two grades being entered in the record, with the average partial grade not being less than 3.0. Unjustified absence from a test results in the loss of that attempt. Each student has the right to two retake colloquiums, which may take place at intervals of no less than 2 days. The final grade for the language course is determined as the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained by the student from the passes of individual semesters and the foreign language exam. A student must attend all classes of their language group. In case of justified absence due to illness, a medical certificate must be submitted no later than 14 days after the justified absence. In case of unjustified absence, the student should contact the instructor who will individually specify how to make up for the absence, within 14 days from the date of absence. Unjustified absence from two classes does not require making up. If the number of unjustified absences exceeds 7, the instructor should refuse to credit the semester, even if some of them were previously made up.
